method.teacher_system: The teacher first explains posture and hand placement in a line dance, then breaks down the core steps in small chunks using counts and repetition, and finally guides the learner through three progressive speeds with music.
method.signature: Using a physical white line on the floor as a visual guide and teaching entirely from a back view so learners can easily mirror the steps without flipping left and right.

practices.what: Breaks the first four steps down step-by-step and repeats them.
Adds more steps to the sequence, building up to nine steps and repeating.
Adds the final steps of the dance, completing the full sequence.
Repeats the accumulated sequence multiple times before adding new steps.
Turns around to show the dance from the back view so learners can follow along.
Practices the full dance at half speed with music.
Practices the full dance at three-quarter speed with music.
Practices the full dance at full speed with music.

beliefs.belief: The teacher believes that anyone can learn the traditional Hasapiko dance by following the core steps.
The teacher believes that learners should be able to control their own pace by rewinding the video as needed.

feelings.response: The teacher reassures the learner that it is okay to rewind the video if they have not grasped the steps.

moments.says: The teacher encourages the learner to feel comfortable rewinding the video if they have not grasped the steps.
The teacher explains the importance of body posture and how to hold oneself before teaching the steps.
The teacher demonstrates how to hold onto a partner's shoulders correctly for the dance.
The teacher breaks down the dance into small, manageable steps to help the learner build up to the full dance.
The teacher points out that the back foot should be lifted off the ground during the rocking motion.
The teacher confirms the learner has learned the dance and suggests practicing at different speeds.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable and in control of their own learning process.
